properties.statement:
AFTER A CLI RESTORE, THE LATENT SURFACE STAYS LATENT FOR THE REST OF THE SESSION, AND THE ONE TOOL IT OFFERS IS THE WRONG ONE. music_graph, fourth pass, 2026-08-15, on the run-book's own documented restore path.

WHAT HAPPENED: the MCP server started against an empty directory, correctly served the latent surface, and said so — 'no design graph has ever been started at .reflow2/graph … exactly one tool is served — reflow2_start_design.' TRUE WHEN PRINTED. False ninety seconds later, once `--import` had built the store. NOTHING RE-PROBES, so every design tool stayed unavailable and the export could not be refreshed from the very session that had just done the restore.

⭐ THE SHARP EDGE IS THE COMBINATION WITH `fact:defect-import-materialises-defaults-so-a-restored-graph-reads-as-changed`. At that moment: the graph exists, the pre-commit hook is BLOCKING commits because the restored store reports itself changed, and THE ONLY TOOL ON OFFER IS THE ONE THAT STARTS A DESIGN — against a directory that now has one. The latent surface's own warning that it is 'easy to accept by accident' is aimed at exactly this situation AND CANNOT BE ACTED ON FROM INSIDE IT. The way out is to restart the client, which is not mentioned anywhere.

THEIR ASKS, in their order of preference: (a) RE-PROBE the graph path when a tool is called and promote latent → full surface in place — 'the latent server already knows the path it is watching'; (b) or have `reflow2_start_design` detect that a store appeared since startup and say 'a design exists here now, restart your client to attach' instead of offering to begin one over the top; (c) or have the latent blurb name the restore command and the restart requirement together, since `--import` is the documented way out of latent mode and currently leaves you stuck in it.

SAME FAMILY AS A TRAP THIS PROJECT ALREADY KNOWS: a rebuilt binary does not replace a running stdio server, and only a full client restart does. THIS SESSION HIT THAT VERSION TODAY — the `subject` field built this afternoon was unreachable from the live server, and the ChangeEvent recording that work had to say so in its own name. THE SURFACE A SESSION BOUND TO AT STARTUP IS NOT RE-EXAMINED, WHICHEVER WAY IT IS WRONG.

WHAT THEY PRAISED ON THE SAME PATH, recorded because it is the counterweight: `--diff <file>` against the live graph with no server running 'answered “did the restore work” completely in one call'. That it runs FILE-AGAINST-STORE rather than file-against-file is what made it usable — there was nothing else to compare to yet — and it is what turned a suspected broken hook into a two-line finding. The run-book's list of what does not travel with a clone was 'accurate on a real second machine, in the right order'.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether re-probing per call has a cost worth measuring, and whether any other surface decision is frozen at startup the same way.
